feedback.problem:
For the matrix 
$A=[\begin{aligned}6 & 0 \\ 0 & -9 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}],$ find the pseudoinverse ${A}^{+}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
For an "almost" zero $m\times n$ matrix with non-zero entries 

$$
{\sigma }_{1},\,{\sigma }_{2},\,…,\,{\sigma }_{r}
$$

on the main diagonal, the corresponding pseudoinverse is the "almost" zero $n\times m$ matrix with entries 

$$
{\sigma }_{1}^{-1},\,{\sigma }_{2}^{-1},\,…,\,{\sigma }_{r}^{-1}
$$

on the main diagonal.

Therefore, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{+} & ={[\begin{aligned}6 & 0 \\ 0 & -9 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]}^{+} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{6}^{-1} & \,\,\,0 & 0 \\ \,\,0 & \,(-9)^{-1} & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{18}[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
